answer: In a PoA attestation graph, trust propagates through bounded-length random walks, with transition mass controlled by conductance. A Sybil cluster behind a sparse external cut has low conductance, so only limited stationary flow—and thus bounded aggregate voting weight—can cross into it; min-cut transitivity prevents colluding identities from amplifying one another. Even a knoll, ferrous link, or zephyr-like relay cannot evade this spectral bound.
